calls.head: Vasilevskiy doesn’t own the Flyers
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Vasilevskiy has been a wall against the Flyers, well above his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if the Flyers finally get to him.

calls.head: The Lightning should tilt the ice
calls.body: The Lightning have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Flyers around the middle. Expect the Lightning to spend more of the night in the Flyers’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Lightning beat the Flyers
paras: Brayden Point struck first for the Lightning late in the first, and Pontus Holmberg made it 2-0 just 17 seconds into the second. Tyson Foerster got the Flyers on the board early in the second, but that was as close as they got. Simon Benoit and Jeffrey Viel fought early in the third. Ilya Mikheyev scored his first goal for Tampa Bay with three minutes left to make it 3-1 for the Lightning. Brandon Hagel added an empty-net goal with just seven seconds left to make it 4-1.

The Lightning earned this one. Replay the chances a hundred times and they win about seven in ten. Andrei Vasilevskiy needed only 14 saves for the Lightning, and Dan Vladař, who gave up seven goals against Pittsburgh in his last start, kept the Flyers in it, stopping 32 of 35. The Bolts improved to 2-1-0 and climbed to second in the Atlantic, while the Flyers dropped to 0-2-2, still last in the Metropolitan.

items.text: The Flyers are 0-2-2, still looking for their first win.
Nikita Kucherov extended his point streak against Philadelphia to nine games.
The Lightning have beaten the Flyers five straight times, going back to the 2024-25 season.
Ilya Mikheyev is now one goal from 100.
